source.title: Improving deep label noise learning with dual active label correction
source.authors: Shaoyuan Li; Ye Shi; Sheng-Jun Huang; Song-Can Chen

record.tranche_reason: Uses the cited memorization effect to select confident instances and reports a qualitative finding about predictions on mislabeled training instances; it does not test the claim versions’ specified fitting or temporal-learning outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that, with early-stopped training, the classifier correctly predicts the true labels of many mislabeled instances. It does not report fitting completely random labels, training error on random labels, fitting unstructured inputs, or the temporal order in which clean and noisy patterns are learned. Reported classification accuracies and transition-matrix estimation results concern the DALC method and are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the cited clean-patterns-first effect to motivate active label correction. Its own early-stopped snapshot does not measure learning order or subsequent memorization, and its method comparisons do not establish the fitting outcomes specified by V1–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors attribute correct true-label predictions on many high-loss mislabeled instances to memorization effects, use this to motivate DALC, and conclude that combining expert labels with confident classifier predictions improves classification and reduces transition-matrix estimation bias.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses early-stopped training and a dual active label correction procedure on noisy-label datasets; it does not apply the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes the finding for CIFAR-10 with 40% symmetric label errors and early-stopped training; it also states that DALC-e converges without overfitting in its CIFAR experiments at noise ratios 40%, 60%, and 80%.

fits_no_version.finding: With early-stopped forward loss correction on CIFAR-10 with 40% symmetric label noise and no queried true labels, correctly labeled instances have smaller losses, and many mislabeled instances receive predictions matching their true labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An early-stopped classifier trained with forward loss correction can recover true labels for many mislabeled training instances under substantial label noise.

record.problems: The relevant finding is qualitative and reports no numeric proportion; Fig. 1c is described without numerical values. Experiments are repeated five times, but standard deviations are omitted from the tables; the paper states their ranges.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Classification-accuracy and transition-matrix comparisons in Tables 1–6 and Figs. 2–3 evaluate the proposed DALC approach or its baselines, not a claim version’s specified behavior.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance under completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep and steadily increasing test error toward chance. Reported test accuracies evaluate label correction methods without establishing perfect noisy-label fitting.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them preserves true-label generalization.

Temporal comparison showing shared real patterns learned before noisy labels and subsequent noise memorization. Figure 1c reports only an early-stopped snapshot; Figure 3 tracks aggregate losses for DALC-e with label correction.

record.verdict_notes: The early-stopped finding is consistent with the motivation behind V6, but does not independently establish its temporal claim. DALC-e's convergence without overfitting under deliberate noise correction does not challenge spontaneous memorization in standard training.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure learning order over training; its early-stopped finding concerns predictions on mislabeled instances.

rows.subject: deep neural network classifier
rows.operation_detail: Describes the training-loss distribution and true-label prediction correctness for training instances under early-stopped training.

conditions.value: early stopped; no extra true labels used

rows.measure: Qualitative training-loss distribution and correctness of predictions relative to groundtruth labels for correctly labeled and mislabeled instances.
rows.value: The correctly labeled instances have much smaller losses than mislabeled ones; for a large proportion of mislabeled instances, the classifier can correctly predict their true labels.
rows.note: Qualitative description of Fig. 1c; does not report a temporal comparison across training or a numeric proportion.
rows.check: The qualitative finding is accurately extracted, but cannot establish temporal learning order. Specify that the classifier uses forward loss correction and, under Section 4.1's CIFAR settings, a depth-40 Wide Residual Network with widening factor 2. No numeric proportion or comparison with later training is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
